question: How many essential controls should I prepare for a flow cytometry sorting experiment using Streptavidin beads with five channels, assuming the detection channels are AF350, GFP, PE, AF647, and AF750?

8.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I would plan on 10 essential controls for a 5-colour sort with those fluorochromes.

For the AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750 panel you need a clean compensation set and a clean gating set. That is:

* 5 single-stain compensation controls, one per reporter. With streptavidin beads you can put each fluor-conjugated streptavidin reagent on beads or a bright single-positive cell population to generate the AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750 spillover matrices.

* 1 unstained / beads-only control to set voltages and establish autofluorescence of the streptavidin beads and the sample background.

* 4 FMO controls for sorting gates. FMOs are used to define the negative boundary in each channel in the presence of the other four fluorochromes. In practice the FMO that lacks AF750 is essentially the unstained/beads-only baseline for the most red channel, so the fifth FMO is redundant with the unstained control you already have for voltage setting. So you need FMOs for AF350-, GFP-, PE- and AF647- while all other four fluorochromes are present.

5 singles + 1 unstained + 4 FMOs = 10 controls, which gives you a compensation matrix, a background baseline for the streptavidin beads, and FMO-defined gates for all five sorting channels without duplication.

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I would plan on 10 essential controls for this 5-channel streptavidin-bead sort.

That breaks down as 1 unstained/bead-only baseline to set autofluorescence and non-specific streptavidin binding, 5 single-stain compensation controls, one for each detection channel AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750, run on streptavidin beads to generate the spectral matrix, and 4 FMO controls for gate setting.

With a 5-fluorophore panel you need an FMO for each channel that has spillover into a neighboring detector to define the positive boundary. In practice the far-red AF750 channel is used as a dump/low spillover channel and its FMO is essentially covered by the unstained/bead-only control, so the conventional n-1 FMO set is sufficient for sorting. 1 + 5 + 4 = 10 controls lets you compensate accurately and set unbiased gates while keeping the sort panel practical.

6.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: For a 5-colour sort you need at least a compensation matrix and a blank to set voltages and autofluorescence.

The streptavidin bead compensation set can be re-used for all of the biotinylated reagents, so the compensation minimum is

* 1 x beads only / unstained cells   = autofluorescence / background and the voltage/baseline
* 5 x single-stain streptavidin bead controls, one for each reporter that will be on the instrument

AF350 , GFP , PE , AF647 , AF750

i.e. 5 single colour compensation controls + 1 blank = 6 compensation related samples.

That is the absolute minimum you can run a sort on. That gives you an n+1 compensation matrix and a negative baseline.

In practice a sort needs gates to be set on biological cells and not on spill-over. For robust, publishable gating you add fluorescence-minus-one controls for the sort gates:

5 FMO controls, one per channel, in addition to the 6 compensation/blank controls.

That is 1 unstained + 5 single-stain compensation beads + 5 FMOs = 11 samples in total that are routinely prepared for a 5-colour sort. The 5 single-stain bead controls and the 1 blank are the essential, non-negotiable controls; the FMOs are the standard best-practice addition for sorting gate definition.

10.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: For a standard 5-colour compensation set up on beads the minimal
compensation set is n fluorochromes + a negative bead baseline.

With Streptavidin / capture beads the compensation control for each detector
is a bead tube that is loaded with a single fluorochrome-conjugated
biotinylated reagent and therefore gives a positive signal in only one
detector and essentially zero in the others. That is one tube per
fluorochrome that you will actually use for compensation.

* AF350  – 1 × streptavidin bead single stain
* GFP    – 1 × streptavidin bead single stain
* PE     – 1 × streptavidin bead single stain
* AF647  – 1 × streptavidin bead single stain
* AF750  – 1 × streptavidin bead single stain

That is 5 single-colour compensation bead tubes. 
In practice a beads-only / unstained bead negative is run in parallel to
set the baseline autofluorescence / bead scatter and to define the
negative population for the compensation matrix.  With the negative
baseline the conventional n+1 set is

5 single stain compensation beads + 1 unstained/beads-only negative = 6
tubes

which is the 5 compensation controls that are commonly quoted as “5
controls, one per channel”. The unstained bead tube is the sixth essential
control and it is the tube that is also used as the sort negative /
autofluorescence reference. If FMO gating controls for the cell sample
itself are required for a sort those are additional to the bead
compensation set.

4.text:
With beads the compensation set can be made completely independent of cells and
you can get away with the compensation set only.

For a 5 fluorochrome panel the compensation matrix is defined by

* 1 unstained / beads-only control to define autofluorescence / bead
  background and the negative reference for each detector, AF350, GFP, PE,
  AF647 and AF750, and
* 1 bright single colour compensation control per fluorochrome that is
  actually seen in the panel.

With streptavidin capture beads the single colour controls are made by
incubating separate aliquots of the beads with a saturating amount of
biotinylated antibody that is conjugated to the fluorochrome of interest and
then with the streptavidin bead reagent. The unstained beads are beads
incubated with the streptavidin reagent only.

Hence the minimal compensation set is

* 1 × unstained / beads-only
* 5 × AF350+, GFP+, PE+, AF647+, AF750+ single-stain beads

= 6 bead controls, 5 of which are the single colour compensation controls.

That is the absolute minimum that will allow a correct compensation matrix
to be calculated and a sort gate to be placed on an unstained background.
For a real sort you will want a fluorescence minus one control for each
channel to set the positive/negative boundaries in the presence of spectral
spill, i.e. 5 FMOs, in addition to the unstained and the 5 single stain
compensation beads, 2n+1 = 11 controls in total, 6 of which are the
compensation-essential set. The isotype / biological negative and a viability
dye control are then added on top of this for a publication quality sort.

12.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Minimum 1 negative + 5 single colour = 6 bead tubes for compensation and baseline setting, i.e. 5 fluorochrome specific compensation controls and 1 unstained bead control.

For a conventional spectral compensation / voltage set up with n fluorochromes you need

* 1 unstained / bead-only control for autofluorescence and instrument baseline
* n single-stain compensation controls, one per detector

With AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750 that is n = 5

* AF350-streptavidin bead single stain
* GFP-streptavidin bead single stain
* PE-streptavidin bead single stain
* AF647-streptavidin bead single stain
* AF750-streptavidin bead single stain
* Unstained streptavidin beads

These 6 tubes are sufficient to set voltages, set the negative population and build an n x n compensation matrix for sorting. In practice for sorting you will normally also run an unstained cell sample and a viability dye control and, for rigorous gate definition, 5 fluorescence-minus-one controls, one per channel, giving 1 unstained cells + 1 viability + 5 single-stains + 5 FMOs = 12 tubes total. The 6 bead controls above are the essential compensation minimum.

13.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I’d plan on 10 essential controls for a 5-color streptavidin-bead sort on AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750.

That is 1 unstained streptavidin bead control to set baseline autofluorescence and sort background, 5 single-stain compensation controls, one for each fluorochrome on bead-bound capture, AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750, to build the compensation matrix, and 4 fluorescence-minus-one controls for gate setting.

The FMOs are typically needed for n-1 panels. For a 5-marker sort you need FMO for AF350+GFP+PE+AF647, FMO for AF350+GFP+PE+AF750, FMO for AF350+GFP+AF647+AF750 and FMO for GFP+PE+AF647+AF750. The FMO that leaves out only AF350 is effectively the unstained bead control in this bead-based system, so it can be collapsed with the unstained. 1 + 5 + 4 = 10 controls to cover autofluorescence, spectral compensation and spillover-based gate placement for sorting.

16.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: At minimum you need an unstained / beads-only baseline and one single colour compensation control for every fluorophore you will put on the machine.

With 5 detection channels

* 1 x beads/streptavidin-beads only / unstained cell control for autofluorescence and for setting the negative boundary and time-zero baseline
* 1 x single-stain compensation control per fluorophore on streptavidin beads, i.e. AF350-biotin-Streptavidin bead, GFP-biotin-Streptavidin bead, PE-biotin-Streptavidin bead, AF647-biotin-Streptavidin bead, AF750-biotin-Streptavidin bead

= 1 + 5 = 6 tubes minimum for compensation and gating.

That is the essential set for a sort. In practice a sorting experiment is run with the 5 single-stain bead controls for spectral unmixing/compensation plus the unstained bead/cell control, and most labs then add the 5 fluorescence-minus-one controls for rigorous gate placement, i.e. 5 FMOs + 5 singles + 1 unstained = 11 tubes in total, the FMOs being the usual best practice for a 5-colour sort.

18.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Minimum compensation set = 6 bead tubes.

For a 5-colour sort the spectral compensation matrix can be built entirely on
streptavidin-capture beads. The essential bead based set is

* 1 × unstained / beads-only streptavidin bead control for autofluorescence/
  background and voltage/base level setting
* 1 × single-color streptavidin bead control per reporter that will be used
  on cells

  * AF350 – biotinylated AF350-conjugate on streptavidin beads
  * GFP – biotinylated GFP-conjugate / GFP-positive bead on streptavidin beads
  * PE – biotinylated PE-conjugate on streptavidin beads
  * AF647 – biotinylated AF647-conjugate on streptavidin beads
  * AF750 – biotinylated AF750-conjugate on streptavidin beads

That is 1 + 5 = 6 tubes for a correct spillover matrix and for setting
detector voltages and thresholds. The unstained bead tube is the negative
control for the bead lot and the five single-stain tubes give the 5 × 5
compensation values for AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750.

In practice a sort is never run on compensation alone. For robust gate
placement you will normally add a biological unstained cell control and
5 fluorescence-minus-one controls, one FMO per channel, 1 FMO = all 5
fluorochromes except the channel of interest. With those gating controls
the rigorous experimental set is 1 unstained cells + 5 single-stain bead
compensation controls + 5 FMOs = 11 tubes, 6 of which are the essential
bead-based compensation controls.

1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Minimum essential for a usable compensation matrix and for setting a negative gate is one bead negative + one single colour compensation control per detection channel.

With 5 detection channels

* 1 x unstained / streptavidin-bead only negative control for autofluorescence / background and for voltage / time gate setting
* 1 x single-stained streptavidin-bead compensation control per fluorochrome

    AF350 single, GFP single, PE single, AF647 single, AF750 single

= 1 + 5 = 6 bead tubes.

Those six tubes are sufficient to build a 5 × 5 compensation matrix and to define an unstained bead negative population in each of AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750. In practice the same streptavidin beads that are used to capture the biotinylated reagents are used for the single colour compensation controls, so the beads themselves serve as the matrix.

For a sorting experiment the recommended best practice is to add fluorescence minus one controls for gate placement, i.e. 5 FMO bead tubes each containing four of the five fluorochromes and lacking one. With FMOs the practical set is 1 unstained + 5 single colour + 5 FMO = 11 tubes, the 6 compensation/negative tubes being the absolute minimum.

3.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: For compensation/sort set-up the absolute minimum you can get away with on the sorter is a beads-only / unstained reference and one single colour compensation reference per reporter that you will put on the machine.

With a 5 colour panel

* 1 x Streptavidin bead only / unstained beads, i.e. beads + buffer, no biotinylated reagent. This is your autofluorescence / background and the reference for voltage and threshold setting and for the unstained cell gate.
* 1 x single stain compensation bead per fluorochrome that will be used in the experiment, on streptavidin beads:

  1. AF350-biotin capture on streptavidin beads
  2. GFP-biotin capture on streptavidin beads
  3. PE-biotin capture on streptavidin beads
  4. AF647-biotin capture on streptavidin beads
  5. AF750-biotin capture on streptavidin beads

That is 5 + 1 = 6 essential bead controls for compensation and for setting a beads-only negative gate. The single stains are what you use to build the 5 x 5 spillover matrix for AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750.

In practice for a sort you will want the rigorous gating set as well:
* 5 x Fluorescence Minus One controls, one FMO per channel, on streptavidin beads, to set positive/negative boundaries in the presence of the other 4 fluorochromes
* a viability dye single stain if a viability dye is used

so 5 single stains + 1 unstained + 5 FMOs = 11 bead controls, plus viability, is the best practice sort panel. The 6 controls above are the non-negotiable compensation / background minimum.

11.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Minimum essential bead set for a 5 colour sort is 1 unstained bead control + 1 single colour compensation control per fluorophore.

* 1 x Streptavidin bead only / unstained autofluorescence control
* 5 x single-stain compensation beads, one for each detection channel:
  AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750

i.e. 5 + 1 = 6 essential bead tubes for compensation and for setting the negative population.

That is the minimum required to be able to compensate the 5 colour panel and to define negative vs positive on the sorter. In practice for a sorting experiment the gating is made robust by also running fluorescence-minus-one controls for each channel so that spread and spill-over into the gate can be judged. That adds 5 FMO bead tubes to the 6 above, 5 single-stain +5 FMO +1 unstained = 11 tubes in total, and is the normal best-practice bead set for a 5-colour sort. If only the strict compensation requirement is counted the essential number is 6 tubes.

9.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I would prepare 10 essential controls for a 5-color Streptavidin bead sort on AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750.

That is 1 unstained/bead autofluorescence baseline to set voltages and negative boundaries, 5 single-stain compensation controls, one per fluorophore, using either singly labeled beads or cells to build the compensation matrix for AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750, and 4 FMO controls to validate the gating strategy for sorting.

The FMO set is effectively n-1 for a panel where the unstained control already provides the all-minus reference, so you need FMOs for AF350-minus, GFP-minus, PE-minus and AF647-minus with AF750 present, and the AF750-minus condition is covered by the unstained baseline. In practice that is 1 + 5 + 4 = 10 controls that are strictly required to set compensation correctly and to define sort gates without spillover artefacts.

5.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: 10 essential controls.

For a 5-color sort with streptavidin bead-based compensation I would prepare 5 single-stain compensation controls and 5 fluorescence-minus-one controls. The single-stain controls are made with streptavidin beads coupled to each reporter — AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750 — to build the compensation matrix for the five detection channels. The five FMOs, each with four of the five reporters and the fifth omitted, are what you actually use to set sort gates and to verify spillover in a sorting experiment. In practice the unstained/beads-only baseline is contained within the FMO series for the last channel, so the minimal essential set for compensation and gating is 5 single-stains + 5 FMOs = 10 controls.

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: For a conventional multicolour sort the minimum set that will let you
compensate the instrument and set a biological negative is

* 1 x unstained / beads-alone negative control
* 1 x single-colour compensation control per reporter that you will put on the
  instrument

With n = 5 reporters that is

n + 1 = 5 single-stain streptavidin-bead compensation controls for
AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750  +  1 unstained streptavidin bead / cell
negative control = 6 controls in total.

Those 6 controls give you a beads-alone baseline for autofluorescence and
scatter and a single-positive spectrum for each of the five detection channels
AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750 so that spill-over compensation matrices can
be calculated for the streptavidin bead system and a negative population can
be defined for sorting.

In practice for a sort the best-practice gating set is the minimum set above
plus a fluorescence-minus-one control for every channel that will be used to
define a sort gate, i.e. 5 FMOs. That gives the commonly quoted 2n+1 best-
practice set, 1 unstained + 5 single-stain compensation + 5 FMO = 11
specimens, 6 of which are strictly required for compensation and a negative
reference.

14.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: For a 5-color sort on AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750 with biotinylated reagents captured on streptavidin beads I would run 10 essential controls.

That is 1 unstained cell control for autofluorescence and baseline gating, 5 single-color compensation controls made with the streptavidin beads matched to each fluorochrome to build the compensation matrix, and 4 independent Fluorescence Minus One controls to set the positive gates. The FMO in which all five fluorochromes are omitted is essentially the unstained control, so it does not add independent information for gate placement. So 1 + 5 + 4 = 10 controls are needed for robust compensation and sorting gate definition.

15.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Minimum compensation set for a 5-colour sort is 1+5 controls.

For spectral compensation you need an autofluorescence / unstained bead reference and one single fluorophore reference per detection channel so that the spillover matrix can be calculated.

* 1 x unstained / Streptavidin-bead only autofluorescence control
* 5 x single-stain compensation controls, one per fluorophore

AF350 single-stain on Streptavidin beads
GFP single-stain on Streptavidin beads
PE single-stain on Streptavidin beads
AF647 single-stain on Streptavidin beads
AF750 single-stain on Streptavidin beads

That is 6 essential compensation controls, 1 + n where n = 5 channels. 

In practice for a sort you will want robust gate placement as well. Best practice is then to add an FMO for each channel, 5 x FMO controls, giving 1 unstained + 5 single-stain + 5 FMO = 11 controls in total for reliable compensation and gating. The 1+5 set is the absolute minimum required to build a compensation matrix for AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750.

17.text:
For a 5 colour sort the compensation matrix and the autofluorescence baseline have to be defined on the same material that you will sort on, in your case streptavidin beads.

* Compensation
Compensation is set with a single fluorochrome signal on the same bead matrix that will be used for the experiment. With 5 detection channels

AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750

you need one single-stained streptavidin-bead control per fluorochrome that is used in the panel. That is

1 × AF350-biotin
1 × GFP-biotin
1 × PE-biotin
1 × AF647-biotin
1 × AF750-biotin

The 5 singles give the spillover matrix for the 5 channels. An unstained / beads only control is required to define autofluorescence and the digital zero for the instrument and for gating on the bead population.

Unstained streptavidin beads + 5 single-stained compensation beads = 6 essential acquisition controls, 5 compensation + 1 negative/autofluorescence.

In practice for cell sorting the gate placement is normally validated with fluorescence-minus-one controls. That is a further 5 FMO bead/cell populations, one per channel, i.e. the full panel minus AF350, minus GFP, minus PE, minus AF647 and minus AF750, in addition to the 6 controls above, 11 controls in total that are used in most core facilities, 12 if the unstained is counted separately from the FMOs. An isotype / biotin-blocked bead control for non-specific streptavidin binding is also normally run for each antibody specificities in a publication quality experiment.

Minimum essential for a usable compensation matrix and for setting a negative gate is one bead negative + one single colour compensation control per detection channel.

With 5 detection channels

* 1 x unstained / streptavidin-bead only negative control for autofluorescence / background and for voltage / time gate setting
* 1 x single-stained streptavidin-bead compensation control per fluorochrome

    AF350 single, GFP single, PE single, AF647 single, AF750 single

= 1 + 5 = 6 bead tubes.

Those six tubes are sufficient to build a 5 × 5 compensation matrix and to define an unstained bead negative population in each of AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750. In practice the same streptavidin beads that are used to capture the biotinylated reagents are used for the single colour compensation controls, so the beads themselves serve as the matrix.

For a sorting experiment the recommended best practice is to add fluorescence minus one controls for gate placement, i.e. 5 FMO bead tubes each containing four of the five fluorochromes and lacking one. With FMOs the practical set is 1 unstained + 5 single colour + 5 FMO = 11 tubes, the 6 compensation/negative tubes being the absolute minimum.
public_text.3:
For compensation/sort set-up the absolute minimum you can get away with on the sorter is a beads-only / unstained reference and one single colour compensation reference per reporter that you will put on the machine.

With a 5 colour panel

* 1 x Streptavidin bead only / unstained beads, i.e. beads + buffer, no biotinylated reagent. This is your autofluorescence / background and the reference for voltage and threshold setting and for the unstained cell gate.
* 1 x single stain compensation bead per fluorochrome that will be used in the experiment, on streptavidin beads:

  1. AF350-biotin capture on streptavidin beads
  2. GFP-biotin capture on streptavidin beads
  3. PE-biotin capture on streptavidin beads
  4. AF647-biotin capture on streptavidin beads
  5. AF750-biotin capture on streptavidin beads

That is 5 + 1 = 6 essential bead controls for compensation and for setting a beads-only negative gate. The single stains are what you use to build the 5 x 5 spillover matrix for AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750.

In practice for a sort you will want the rigorous gating set as well:
* 5 x Fluorescence Minus One controls, one FMO per channel, on streptavidin beads, to set positive/negative boundaries in the presence of the other 4 fluorochromes
* a viability dye single stain if a viability dye is used

so 5 single stains + 1 unstained + 5 FMOs = 11 bead controls, plus viability, is the best practice sort panel. The 6 controls above are the non-negotiable compensation / background minimum.
public_text.11:
Minimum essential bead set for a 5 colour sort is 1 unstained bead control + 1 single colour compensation control per fluorophore.

* 1 x Streptavidin bead only / unstained autofluorescence control
* 5 x single-stain compensation beads, one for each detection channel:
  AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750

i.e. 5 + 1 = 6 essential bead tubes for compensation and for setting the negative population.

That is the minimum required to be able to compensate the 5 colour panel and to define negative vs positive on the sorter. In practice for a sorting experiment the gating is made robust by also running fluorescence-minus-one controls for each channel so that spread and spill-over into the gate can be judged. That adds 5 FMO bead tubes to the 6 above, 5 single-stain +5 FMO +1 unstained = 11 tubes in total, and is the normal best-practice bead set for a 5-colour sort. If only the strict compensation requirement is counted the essential number is 6 tubes.
public_text.9:
I would prepare 10 essential controls for a 5-color Streptavidin bead sort on AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750.

That is 1 unstained/bead autofluorescence baseline to set voltages and negative boundaries, 5 single-stain compensation controls, one per fluorophore, using either singly labeled beads or cells to build the compensation matrix for AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750, and 4 FMO controls to validate the gating strategy for sorting.

The FMO set is effectively n-1 for a panel where the unstained control already provides the all-minus reference, so you need FMOs for AF350-minus, GFP-minus, PE-minus and AF647-minus with AF750 present, and the AF750-minus condition is covered by the unstained baseline. In practice that is 1 + 5 + 4 = 10 controls that are strictly required to set compensation correctly and to define sort gates without spillover artefacts.
public_text.5:
10 essential controls.

For a 5-color sort with streptavidin bead-based compensation I would prepare 5 single-stain compensation controls and 5 fluorescence-minus-one controls. The single-stain controls are made with streptavidin beads coupled to each reporter — AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750 — to build the compensation matrix for the five detection channels. The five FMOs, each with four of the five reporters and the fifth omitted, are what you actually use to set sort gates and to verify spillover in a sorting experiment. In practice the unstained/beads-only baseline is contained within the FMO series for the last channel, so the minimal essential set for compensation and gating is 5 single-stains + 5 FMOs = 10 controls.

public_text.14:
For a 5-color sort on AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750 with biotinylated reagents captured on streptavidin beads I would run 10 essential controls.

1.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The question is about the number of essential controls for a 5-channel Streptavidin-bead sort with AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750.

Consensus points from round 0:
* Compensation is done on the same matrix that will be sorted, i.e. streptavidin beads.
* Minimal compensation set is n+1: 1 unstained/beads-only autofluorescence/baseline control + 1 single-stain compensation control per fluorochrome.
* For 5 channels that is 1 + 5 = 6 bead tubes: unstained streptavidin beads + AF350 single, GFP single, PE single, AF647 single, AF750 single. These give autofluorescence baseline, voltage/threshold setting and a 5×5 spillover matrix.
* The single stains are made by capturing biotinylated fluorochrome-conjugated reagents on streptavidin beads.

Disagreement / competing interpretations about what is “essential” for a sorting experiment:
* Strict compensation-minimum camp: Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,16,17,18,3,4,6,7 state the absolute non-negotiable minimum is 6 tubes, with 5 single-stains +1 unstained. They note that 5 FMOs +1 unstained +5 singles =11 is normal best practice for robust gate placement, but FMOs are an addition.
* FMO-essential camp: Colleagues 13,14,2,5,8,9 argue FMOs are essential for sorting gate definition, not just best practice. They propose 1 unstained +5 singles +FMOs.
  * Several of them collapse one FMO with the unstained control, counting only 4 independent FMOs for a 5-marker panel, giving 1+5+4=10 controls. Rationale: the all-minus/FMO that lacks the last channel e.g. AF750 is essentially the unstained/beads-only baseline, so it does not add independent information.
  * Colleague 2,8,9 specifically say AF750 is a dump/low spillover channel and its FMO is covered by unstained.
* Variation in counting: Some quote 11 controls as 1 unstained +5 singles +5 FMOs, 2n+1. Others quote 10 controls as 1 unstained +5 singles +4 FMOs.

Unresolved for me:
* Precise definition of “essential” in the question: does essential mean strictly required to calculate compensation and run the sorter, i.e. 6 tubes, or does it mean essential for a reliable sort with properly placed gates, i.e. include FMOs?
* Whether the unstained control can be considered equivalent to the all-minus FMO and therefore counted only once. Most who propose 10 controls adopt that collapse.
* Whether viability dye, isotype/biotin-blocked bead controls, or unstained cells should be added beyond bead controls.

Current understanding: Minimal compensation-able set is unambiguously 6 bead tubes. The practical sort set most labs use is 11 tubes with FMOs. A middle position advocated by several colleagues is 10 essential controls when one FMO is merged with unstained.

No corrections or factual errors spotted in the channel list. All colleagues agree on the five fluorochromes and the bead-based compensation strategy.

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The question is about essential controls for a 5-channel Streptavidin-bead sort on AF350, GFP, PE, AF647, AF750.

Core consensus from round 0:
* Compensation matrix requires one single-stain bead control per fluorochrome plus an unstained/beads-only negative/baseline.
* That is n+1 = 5 single-stain streptavidin bead compensation tubes + 1 unstained bead tube = 6 bead tubes minimum to build a 5×5 spillover matrix and set voltages/autofluorescence.
* The single-stains are AF350, GFP, PE, AF647, AF750 on streptavidin beads; the unstained is beads + streptavidin only.

Disagreement / nuance about “essential for sorting”:
* Majority view: 6 tubes are the absolute/ non-negotiable compensation minimum. Best practice for sorting adds fluorescence-minus-one gating controls.
* Best practice numbers quoted: 1 unstained + 5 single-stain + 5 FMO = 11 tubes total. FMOs are 5 tubes each missing one fluorochrome, used to define positive/negative boundaries in presence of spillover.
* Minority view: 10 essential controls for sorting. Argument: the all-minus/FMO for the far-red AF750 channel is essentially redundant with the unstained/beads-only baseline, so FMOs needed are 4 not 5. Counting 1 unstained + 5 singles + 4 FMOs = 10. Colleagues 13,14,2,5,8,9 advance this; colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,16,17,18,3,4,6,7 keep the 11-tube best-practice count.
* Some also mention additional practical controls: unstained cells, viability dye, isotype/biotin-blocked non-specific binding control, but these are beyond bead compensation set.

Unresolved: whether “essential” means strictly compensation-capable 6 tubes, or compensation + robust gate definition. The phrasing “for a flow cytometry sorting experiment” pushes toward including FMO gating; the literature commonly quotes 2n+1 = 11 for n=5.

My current synthesis: minimum mathematically required is 6 bead tubes. With sorting gate validation, the practical essential set is 11 tubes, with a plausible 10-tube reduction if the AF750-minus FMO is merged with unstained. Need to decide which definition the question intends.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The question is about number of essential controls for a 5-channel streptavidin-bead sort with AF350, GFP, PE, AF647, AF750.

Public round 0 shows a clear split on what “essential” means.

Compensation minimum consensus:
* 1 unstained / streptavidin-beads-only autofluorescence / background / voltage baseline
* 1 single-stain streptavidin-bead compensation control per fluorochrome = 5
Total = 1 + 5 = 6 bead tubes. This is sufficient to build a 5×5 spillover matrix and define a negative gate. This view is expressed by Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,16,17,18,3,4,6,7.

Best-practice sorting addition:
Most of those colleagues add fluorescence-minus-one controls for robust gate placement: 5 FMOs + 1 unstained + 5 singles = 11 tubes, with 6 being the non-negotiable compensation minimum.

Alternative essential count:
Colleagues 13,14,2,5,8,9 argue FMOs are essential for sorting, but count 1 unstained + 5 singles + 4 FMOs = 10. Rationale: the FMO that lacks AF750 is essentially the unstained/beads-only baseline, so it is redundant and can be collapsed, leaving FMOs for AF350-, GFP-, PE-, AF647- only. They call 10 the essential set for compensation + gate definition.

Unresolved:
Whether “essential” = compensation-only minimum 6, or compensation + gating. If gating is required for a sort, FMOs are argued necessary; disagreement remains on 10 vs 11 due to counting of the all-minus condition. No disagreement on the 5 single-stain bead controls per channel and the need for an unstained bead baseline on the same streptavidin matrix.

I am retaining both the strict 6-tube compensation minimum and the practical 11-tube best-practice set, and noting the 10-tube variant where the unstained control is considered to cover the AF750-minus FMO.

17.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: Round 0 discussion on essential bead controls for a 5-channel streptavidin-bead sort: AF350, GFP, PE, AF647, AF750.

Consensus core:
* Compensation must be done on the same matrix as the experiment, i.e., streptavidin beads capturing biotinylated reagents.
* Minimum compensation set is n single-stain bead controls + 1 unstained/beads-only baseline.
  * 5 single-stain streptavidin bead controls: AF350 single, GFP single, PE single, AF647 single, AF750 single.
  * 1 unstained streptavidin bead / beads-only control for autofluorescence/background, voltage/time gate setting and negative reference.
  = 1 + 5 = 6 tubes. This is repeatedly stated as the absolute minimum for a 5x5 spillover matrix and for defining a negative population.

Best-practice extension:
* Most colleagues add fluorescence-minus-one controls for robust sort gate placement.
* Typical quoting: 1 unstained + 5 single-stain + 5 FMO = 11 tubes, the 6 compensation/negative tubes being the non-negotiable minimum, FMOs being standard best practice for sorting.

Disagreement on “essential” for sorting:
* Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,16,17,18,3,4,6,7: essential = 6 bead tubes for compensation + negative. FMOs are best practice, not strictly essential for compensation.
* Colleagues 13,14,2,8,9: argue essential for a sort includes gating, so 1 unstained +5 singles + FMOs. They propose 10 controls by collapsing the AF750-minus FMO with the unstained baseline, i.e., 1+5+4=10. Rationale: FMO lacking all five is the unstained control; AF750 is often a dump/low-spillover channel so its FMO is redundant.
* Colleague 5: proposes 10 essential as 5 single-stains +5 FMOs, with unstained contained within FMO series.

Unresolved/points to track:
* Definition of “essential” in the question: minimum to build compensation matrix vs minimum to reliably set sort gates.
* Whether unstained is counted separately from the all-minus FMO.
* Whether viability / isotype / biological unstained cell controls are required beyond bead controls. Some colleagues mention them as additional.

Current understanding:
Bead-based compensation minimum is unambiguously 6 tubes. Whether FMOs are deemed essential for a sorting experiment splits the group between 6 vs 10/11. Need clarification on intent of “essential controls” – compensation only vs compensation + gate definition.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The deliberation is centered on the definition of “essential” for a 5-channel streptavidin-bead sort: AF350, GFP, PE, AF647, AF750.

The dominant consensus for the strict compensation minimum is n+1:
* 1 × unstained / streptavidin-bead only / beads-only autofluorescence baseline for voltage, threshold and negative population definition
* 1 × single-stain streptavidin-bead compensation control per fluorochrome = 5 singles
= 1 + 5 = 6 bead tubes. This set is sufficient to build a 5 × 5 spillover matrix and define an unstained bead negative in each detector. Multiple colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,16,17,18,3,4,6,7 state this as the non-negotiable compensation minimum.

Disagreement is about sorting gate definition:
* Best-practice camp: add FMOs. Commonly quoted 2n+1 = 1 unstained + 5 singles + 5 FMOs = 11 tubes, sometimes plus viability / isotype. Colleagues 1,11,12,15,16,17,18,3,4,6,7 cite this.
* FMO-essential camp: FMOs are required for robust sort gate placement, yielding >6 controls. Two variants:
  - 1 unstained + 5 singles + 5 FMOs = 10-11. Colleague 5 counts unstained as contained in FMO series, so 5 singles + 5 FMOs =10 essential.

Colleagues 13,14,2,8,9 advocate this 10-control essential set: 1 baseline, 5 compensation singles, 4 independent FMOs for AF350-, GFP-, PE-, AF647- with the AF750-minus condition covered by unstained.

No colleague disputes the 5 single-stain bead controls + 1 unstained bead baseline as the compensation core. The open question is whether FMOs count as essential for a sorting experiment vs best practice, and whether the unstained control is redundant with one FMO, leading to 6 vs 10 vs 11 controls. PRIVATE REFLECTION: Round 0 discussion centers on what counts as “essential” for a 5-channel streptavidin-bead sort on AF350, GFP, PE, AF647, AF750.

* 1 × single-stain streptavidin-bead compensation control per fluorochrome, i.e. AF350 single, GFP single, PE single, AF647 single, AF750 single

Best-practice sorting addition is FMOs:
* Most colleagues add 5 fluorescence-minus-one bead/cell controls, one per channel, for rigorous positive/negative gate placement in the presence of spillover. Colleagues 1,11,12,16,17,18,3,4,6,7 explicitly state 11 is the normal best-practice sort set, sometimes + viability/un-stained cells.

* Colleague 5 phrases it as 5 singles + 5 FMOs =10 because the unstained is “contained within” the FMO series.

* Whether the question’s “essential controls” means strict compensation minimum 6, or compensation + robust gating. If gating is required for sorting, FMOs are arguably essential.

My current understanding: consensus minimum for compensation is 6 tubes. There is a split between 11 tubes best practice with 5 FMOs, and 10 tubes with 4 FMOs by collapsing one FMO with unstained. No strong evidence yet that the question demands viability or cell unstained beyond bead controls.

reflection_text.1:
The question is about the number of essential controls for a 5-channel Streptavidin-bead sort with AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750.

Consensus points from round 0:
* Compensation is done on the same matrix that will be sorted, i.e. streptavidin beads.
* Minimal compensation set is n+1: 1 unstained/beads-only autofluorescence/baseline control + 1 single-stain compensation control per fluorochrome.
* For 5 channels that is 1 + 5 = 6 bead tubes: unstained streptavidin beads + AF350 single, GFP single, PE single, AF647 single, AF750 single. These give autofluorescence baseline, voltage/threshold setting and a 5×5 spillover matrix.
* The single stains are made by capturing biotinylated fluorochrome-conjugated reagents on streptavidin beads.

Disagreement / competing interpretations about what is “essential” for a sorting experiment:
* Strict compensation-minimum camp: Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,16,17,18,3,4,6,7 state the absolute non-negotiable minimum is 6 tubes, with 5 single-stains +1 unstained. They note that 5 FMOs +1 unstained +5 singles =11 is normal best practice for robust gate placement, but FMOs are an addition.
* FMO-essential camp: Colleagues 13,14,2,5,8,9 argue FMOs are essential for sorting gate definition, not just best practice. They propose 1 unstained +5 singles +FMOs.
  * Several of them collapse one FMO with the unstained control, counting only 4 independent FMOs for a 5-marker panel, giving 1+5+4=10 controls. Rationale: the all-minus/FMO that lacks the last channel e.g. AF750 is essentially the unstained/beads-only baseline, so it does not add independent information.
  * Colleague 2,8,9 specifically say AF750 is a dump/low spillover channel and its FMO is covered by unstained.
* Variation in counting: Some quote 11 controls as 1 unstained +5 singles +5 FMOs, 2n+1. Others quote 10 controls as 1 unstained +5 singles +4 FMOs.

Unresolved for me:
* Precise definition of “essential” in the question: does essential mean strictly required to calculate compensation and run the sorter, i.e. 6 tubes, or does it mean essential for a reliable sort with properly placed gates, i.e. include FMOs?
* Whether the unstained control can be considered equivalent to the all-minus FMO and therefore counted only once. Most who propose 10 controls adopt that collapse.
* Whether viability dye, isotype/biotin-blocked bead controls, or unstained cells should be added beyond bead controls.

Current understanding: Minimal compensation-able set is unambiguously 6 bead tubes. The practical sort set most labs use is 11 tubes with FMOs. A middle position advocated by several colleagues is 10 essential controls when one FMO is merged with unstained.

No corrections or factual errors spotted in the channel list. All colleagues agree on the five fluorochromes and the bead-based compensation strategy.

reflection_text.7:
The question is about essential controls for a 5-channel Streptavidin-bead sort on AF350, GFP, PE, AF647, AF750.

Core consensus from round 0:

* Compensation minimum is universally agreed: 1 unstained / beads-only autofluorescence baseline + 1 single-stain streptavidin bead control per fluorophore.
* With n=5, that is 1 + 5 = 6 bead tubes.
  * 1 x Streptavidin bead only / unstained for autofluorescence, voltage/threshold, bead scatter and negative population definition.
  * 1 x AF350 single-stain on beads
  * 1 x GFP single-stain on beads
  * 1 x PE single-stain on beads
  * 1 x AF647 single-stain on beads
  * 1 x AF750 single-stain on beads
* Those 6 tubes are sufficient to build a 5×5 spillover compensation matrix and define a negative reference.

Disagreement is about what counts as “essential” for a sorting experiment vs strictly for compensation.

* Majority view, Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,16,17,18,3,4,6,7: strict minimum =6. Best practice for sorting adds fluorescence-minus-one controls for gate placement. That is 5 FMOs + 1 unstained + 5 singles = 11 tubes total, 6 being the non-negotiable compensation set. Some note additional unstained cells, viability dye, isotype/block controls for publication quality.

* Minority / alternative view, Colleagues 13,14,2,5,8,9: argue FMOs are essential for sorting gate definition, not just best practice. They count 1 unstained +5 singles +4 FMOs =10. The reasoning is that the FMO that omits AF750 is effectively the unstained/beads-only control, so the all-minus condition is already covered and does not need a separate FMO. They therefore collapse one FMO with the unstained, giving 1+5+4=10 “essential” controls for compensation + gating.

Arguments for the 6-tube minimum: compensation matrix and negative baseline can be done on beads alone; FMOs are for gate robustness, not instrument setup.

Arguments for 10/11: sorting requires unbiased positive/negative boundaries in the presence of spillover; FMOs are standard for sort gate placement. Debate is whether the AF750-minus FMO is redundant with unstained.

Unresolved for me:

I think the practical essential set for a sort with streptavidin beads on AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750 is 10 controls, not 11.

You need three things to be able to sort: a baseline autofluorescence/bead background, a compensation matrix built on the same bead matrix you will sort on, and FMO-defined negative boundaries for gate placement in the presence of spillover.

That is:

* 5 x single-stain compensation controls on streptavidin beads, one per detection channel: AF350 single, GFP single, PE single, AF647 single, AF750 single. Those five, together with the unstained, give the 5x5 spillover matrix for the bead system.

The unstained bead control already provides the all-minus reference for that channel, so counting it again as a separate FMO is double counting.

FMO-essential / collapsed-count camp, Colleagues 13,14,2,5,8,9:

* Therefore non-redundant FMO set is AF350-, GFP-, PE-, AF647- only.

Intermediate / both-count statements:
* Colleague 10,11,12,15,16,17,18 note formal count is 11, but 10 is often quoted when unstained is taken as the AF750-minus FMO.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: Round 1 discussion confirms the bead-based compensation core and sharpens the essential vs best-practice split for a 5-channel streptavidin-bead sort on AF350, GFP, PE, AF647, AF750.

Compensation minimum – essentially unanimous
* 1 × unstained/streptavidin-bead-only/autofluorescence baseline for voltage/threshold/digital zero and negative reference in all five detectors
* 1 × single-stain streptavidin-bead compensation control per fluorochrome: AF350 single, GFP single, PE single, AF647 single, AF750 single
= 1 + 5 = 6 bead tubes. This builds the 5×5 spillover matrix on the same bead matrix that will be sorted on. Cited as non-negotiable by Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,16,17,18,3,4,6,7.

Sorting gate definition – FMOs
* Compensation alone does not set a sort gate. Best practice for sorting is to add fluorescence-minus-one controls for unbiased positive/negative boundary placement in the presence of spillover.
* Formal 2n+1 counting: 1 unstained + 5 singles + 5 FMOs = 11 tubes. FMOs: -AF350, -GFP, -PE, -AF647, -AF750 each with the other four fluorochromes on beads. This is the conventional core-facility SOP quoted by Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,16,17,18,3,4,6,7.

Redundancy dispute on FMOs
* Colleagues 2,5,8,9,13,14 argue for 10 essential controls by collapsing one FMO with the unstained baseline. Argument: the all-minus condition is already provided by the unstained bead control; the AF750-minus FMO contains AF350+GFP+PE+AF647 and is claimed to be functionally equivalent to beads-only for the far-red/dump channel with minimal spillover. Counting: 1 unstained + 5 singles + 4 independent FMOs = 10. Colleague 13 explicitly collapses AF750-minus; Colleague 8/9 collapse AF750-minus; Colleague 13 also notes alternative collapse of AF350-minus.
* Counter-argument by Colleagues 10,11,16,7,17,18: an FMO -AF750 still contains AF350+GFP+PE+AF647 signal and therefore shows spillover into the AF750 detector, which is not the same as unstained beads-only. Unstained ≠ FMO. With the all-minus condition kept distinct the practical essential sorting set is 11 tubes. Colleague 10 notes the 10-control count is a collapsed/practicable counting, 11 is the formal count.

Evidence retained
* Streptavidin beads allow compensation to be done bead-only; the same bead matrix can be used for singles and FMOs.
* Unstained bead control is beads-only background for autofluorescence and non-specific streptavidin binding, also used as negative reference for compensation matrix.
* FMOs are for gate placement, not strictly required for matrix calculation.

Unresolved / open
* Whether the question’s “essential” means strict compensation minimum 6 tubes, or compensation + robust gating for sorting.

* Whether additional cell-based controls - unstained cells, viability dye, isotype/biotin-blocked bead control for non-specific binding - are required beyond bead controls for a sort. Some colleagues mention them as practical extras but not part of the bead compensation essential set.

Current understanding: consensus minimum for compensation is 6 tubes. There is a strong majority for 11 tubes as standard essential for sorting with 5 FMOs. A minority practical view holds 10 tubes by collapsing the AF750-minus FMO with the unstained bead baseline. No strong evidence yet that the question demands viability or cell unstained beyond bead controls.

reflection_text.1:
The question is about number of essential controls for a 5-channel Streptavidin-bead sort with AF350, GFP, PE, AF647, AF750.

Consensus that remains stable across round 0 and round 1:
* Compensation must be done on the same matrix that will be sorted, i.e. streptavidin beads.
* Minimal compensation-able set is n+1: 1 unstained/beads-only autofluorescence/baseline + 1 single-stain compensation control per fluorochrome.
* For 5 channels that is 1 + 5 = 6 bead tubes: unstained streptavidin beads + AF350 single, GFP single, PE single, AF647 single, AF750 single. These give autofluorescence baseline, voltage/threshold setting and a 5×5 spillover matrix. Singles are made by capturing biotinylated fluorochrome-conjugated reagents on streptavidin beads.

Disagreement persists about what “essential” means for a sorting experiment.

Strict compensation-minimum camp, Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,16,17,18,3,4,6,7:
* Absolute non-negotiable minimum = 6 tubes.
* Best practice for sorting adds FMOs: 1 unstained +5 singles +5 FMOs = 11 = 2n+1.
* FMOs are standard essential for unbiased gate placement in presence of spillover. Colleague 7,16 explicitly argue AF750-minus FMO is not equivalent to unstained because AF750-minus still contains AF350+GFP+PE+AF647 and shows spillover into AF750, whereas unstained shows zero signal.

FMO-essential / collapsed-count camp, Colleagues 13,14,2,5,8,9:
* Argue FMOs are essential for sorting gate definition, not just best practice.
* Propose 1 unstained +5 singles +4 FMOs =10 controls.
* Rationale for collapse: the all-minus / FMO that lacks the last channel e.g. AF750-minus is essentially the unstained/beads-only baseline for this bead system. AF750 is far-red/dump/low spillover, its FMO does not add independent spillover information for gate setting, so AF750-minus is covered by unstained.
* Therefore non-redundant FMO set is AF350-, GFP-, PE-, AF647- only.

Intermediate / both-count statements:
* Colleague 10,11,12,15,16,17,18 note formal count is 11, but 10 is often quoted when unstained is taken as the AF750-minus FMO.
* Colleague 11: 10-control count is same 1+5+5 set with all-minus FMO collapsed into unstained.
* Colleague 16: AF750-minus FMO still contains AF350/GFP/PE/AF647 signal and is therefore not equivalent to unstained beads-only; practical essential sorting set is 11.

Unresolved for me:
* Precise definition of “essential” in the question: strictly required to calculate compensation and run sorter =6, vs essential for reliable sort with properly placed gates = includes FMOs.
* Whether unstained control can be considered equivalent to the all-minus FMO and therefore counted only once. Majority of colleagues treat them as distinct; minority collapse for AF750.
* Whether viability dye, isotype/biotin-blocked bead controls, or unstained cells should be added beyond bead controls. Mentioned as additional best practice but not core to bead compensation debate.

Current understanding:
Minimal compensation-able set is unambiguously 6 bead tubes. The practical sort set most labs use is 11 tubes with FMOs. A middle position advocated by several colleagues is 10 essential controls when one FMO is merged with unstained, specifically AF750-minus. No corrections or factual errors spotted in channel list. Discussion has not shifted the fundamental n+1 consensus, only the FMO counting interpretation.

No new evidence contradicting earlier round. Belief remains that 6 is the strict minimum, 11 is the conventional teaching, 10 is the non-redundant practical claim for this panel because of AF750 dump channel.
reflection_text.3:
The bead-based compensation core is stable across rounds. Minimum to build a 5×5 spillover matrix on the streptavidin bead matrix is n+1: 1 unstained/streptavidin-bead-only autofluorescence/baseline + 1 single-stain compensation bead per detector = 1 + 5 = 6 bead tubes for AF350, GFP, PE, AF647, AF750. Those six tubes set voltages, define bead autofluorescence negative, and allow correct compensation. This is the non-negotiable compensation minimum agreed by colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,16,17,18,3,4,6,7.

For a sort, gate placement in the presence of spillover is the dispute. Standard best-practice teaching is 2n+1: 1 unstained + 5 single-stain compensation + 5 FMO bead tubes = 11 tubes. The FMOs are AF350-, GFP-, PE-, AF647-, AF750- with the other four fluorochromes present, used to define positive/negative boundaries free of spillover. Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,16,17,18,3,4,6,7 hold this as the essential sorting set, with the 6-tube set as the absolute compensation core.

Minority practical view, advanced by colleagues 13,14,2,5,8,9, collapses the all-minus reference. Argument: AF750 is the far-red/dump/low-spillover channel; the AF750-minus FMO containing AF350+GFP+PE+AF647 is functionally indistinguishable from the beads-only unstained baseline for gate setting, so the all-minus condition is already covered by the unstained bead control. That yields 1 unstained + 5 singles + 4 independent FMOs = 10 essential non-redundant controls. Some also note unstained cells, viability dye, isotype/biotin-blocked non-specific binding controls are additional but beyond the bead compensation set.

Counter-argument from colleagues 16,7: an AF750-minus FMO still contains AF350+GFP+PE+AF647 signal and spillover into the AF750 detector, therefore it is not equivalent to an unstained beads-only tube; the all-minus condition is distinct from any FMO.

Unresolved: whether “essential for a sorting experiment” means strictly compensation-capable 6 tubes, or compensation + robust spillover-aware gating. The phrasing pushes toward the latter. Literature/core SOP convention is 2n+1 = 11 for n=5, with 10 as a defensible non-redundant bead-specific reduction if the AF750-minus FMO is merged with unstained. My current synthesis retains 6 as the mathematical minimum, 11 as the conventional essential sorting best practice, and 10 as the plausible non-redundant practical count for this bead panel.

* 1 x single-stain streptavidin-bead compensation control per fluorochrome: AF350, GFP, PE, AF647, AF750
= 1 + 5 = 6 bead tubes, sufficient for a 5×5 spillover matrix on the same bead matrix that will be sorted. This n+1 set is cited by Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,16,17,18,3,4,6,7.

Disagreement is now fully about what counts as essential for a sorting experiment beyond compensation.

Best-practice / textbook camp: compensation minimum + FMO gating = 2n+1.
1 unstained + 5 singles + 5 FMOs = 11 tubes. FMOs are AF350-, GFP-, PE-, AF647-, AF750- each with the other four fluorochromes present. Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,16,17,18,3,4,6,7 state this, with Colleague 7 explicitly arguing unstained ≠ FMO -AF750 because FMO -AF750 still contains AF350+GFP+PE+AF647 and therefore shows spillover into the AF750 detector, not equivalent to zero-signal unstained.

FMO-essential / non-redundant camp: 1 unstained +5 singles +4 independent FMOs =10 essential tubes.
Argument: the all-minus condition is already provided by the unstained bead control. For this panel AF750 is the far-red/dump low-spillover channel; FMO AF750- with AF350+GFP+PE+AF647 present is functionally indistinguishable from unstained beads for gate setting, so the AF750-minus FMO duplicates the unstained baseline. Independent FMOs needed are AF350-, GFP-, PE-, AF647-, with AF750 present. That yields 1+5+4=10. * Single-stain bead controls are non-negotiable for matrix calculation.

1.text:
For a streptavidin-capture sort the spillover matrix has to be built on the same bead matrix that will be sorted on.

Compensation / instrument baseline minimum on beads
* 1 x Streptavidin bead only / unstained bead autofluorescence baseline for voltage, threshold/time gate and the digital zero/negative reference in AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750
* 1 x single-stain streptavidin-bead compensation control per reporter
  AF350-biotin on beads
  GFP-biotin on beads
  PE-biotin on beads
  AF647-biotin on beads
  AF750-biotin on beads

= 1 + 5 = 6 bead tubes. Those 6 tubes are sufficient to build a 5×5 spillover matrix for AF350, GFP, PE, AF647, AF750 and to define an unstained bead negative population. That is the non-negotiable n+1 compensation minimum.

Compensation alone does not set a sort gate. A sort gate has to be placed on spillover-corrected data and the positive/negative boundary in each channel has to be defined in the presence of the other four fluorochromes. That is an FMO.

Best-practice essential sorting set on beads
* 1 unstained / beads-only
* 5 single-stain compensation beads
* 5 FMO bead tubes, one per channel, made with four of the five biotinylated reagents on streptavidin beads
  FMO AF350- + GFP+PE+AF647+AF750
  FMO GFP- + AF350+PE+AF647+AF750
  FMO PE- + AF350+GFP+AF647+AF750
  FMO AF647- + AF350+GFP+PE+AF750
  FMO AF750- + AF350+GFP+PE+AF647

= 1 + 5 + 5 = 11 tubes, the 2n+1 set for n =5.

The 6-tube n+1 set is the absolute compensation/negative reference minimum. The additional 5 FMOs are the standard essential gating controls for an unbiased sort. The 10-tube non-redundant count that collapses the AF750-minus FMO into the unstained bead baseline is a practical shorthand for this panel, but formally the FMO -AF750 still contains AF350+GFP+PE+AF647 signal and is not identical to beads-only. Conventional core-facility SOP and teaching therefore quote the full 11-tube essential sorting set, 6 of which are the strictly required compensation controls.

3.text:
For a streptavidin bead capture panel the compensation matrix has to be built on the bead matrix that will be sorted on.

Compensation / instrument baseline, non-negotiable on beads
* 1 x streptavidin bead only / unstained bead autofluorescence baseline for voltage, time gate and digital zero in AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750
* 1 x single-stain streptavidin bead compensation control per detection channel
  AF350-biotin on streptavidin beads
  GFP-biotin on streptavidin beads
  PE-biotin on streptavidin beads
  AF647-biotin on streptavidin beads
  AF750-biotin on streptavidin beads

1 + 5 = 6 bead tubes. Those six tubes are sufficient to build a 5 × 5 spillover matrix for AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750 and to define an unstained bead negative reference. That is the n+1 compensation minimum.

A sort is not compensation alone. Gate placement has to be defined in the presence of spill-over from the other four fluorochromes. That requires Fluorescence Minus One gating controls on the same bead matrix.

* 1 unstained / beads-only
* 5 single-stain compensation beads
* 5 FMO bead tubes, one per channel
  FMO AF350- with GFP+PE+AF647+AF750
  FMO GFP- with AF350+PE+AF647+AF750
  FMO PE- with AF350+GFP+AF647+AF750
  FMO AF647- with AF350+GFP+PE+AF750
  FMO AF750- with AF350+GFP+PE+AF647

= 1 + 5 + 5 = 11 tubes, the 2n+1 best practice set for n = 5.

The AF750-minus FMO is not equivalent to the unstained beads-only tube. Where sorting changes things is unbiased gate placement in the presence of spillover. The textbook best-practice counting is 1 unstained + 5 singles + 5 FMOs = 11 = 2n+1, and that is what most core SOPs list for a 5-colour sort.

For this specific streptavidin-bead panel with AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750 the 11 tube list does double count the all-minus reference. The unstained streptavidin bead control is already the all-minus baseline for autofluorescence and bead background and it is the negative reference used for voltage setting in every detector.

The AF750-minus FMO in a bead capture system is AF350+GFP+PE+AF647 on streptavidin beads with AF750 omitted. AF750 is the far-red/dump end of the panel with minimal spillover into AF350/GFP/PE/AF647 and essentially negligible bead autofluorescence in that channel. In practice the AF750-minus bead population is indistinguishable from the unstained beads-only baseline for setting the negative boundary in the other four detectors, and the AF750 positive boundary itself is set against the unstained bead autofluorescence reference we already run for compensation.

That means the independent, non-redundant FMO gating controls for sort gate definition are:
* FMO AF350- with GFP+PE+AF647+AF750
* FMO GFP- with AF350+PE+AF647+AF750
* FMO PE- with AF350+GFP+AF647+AF750
* FMO AF647- with AF350+GFP+PE+AF750

Four FMOs where spillover from the other four fluorochromes actually moves the gate.

So the essential, non-duplicative acquisition set for compensation + spillover-aware sorting on this bead matrix is:

1 unstained/beads-only + 5 single-stain compensation beads + 4 independent FMOs = 10 controls.

The 1+5+5 = 11 count is the conventional textbook best-practice checklist and it is useful for completeness, but the unstained bead control is already serving as the effective all-minus / AF750-minus reference for this panel, so the strictly essential practical set is 10 tubes without redundant acquisition.

I think we’re converging on the compensation core and that’s the right place to anchor the discussion.

We can all agree on the bead-based n+1 minimum:
* 1 x streptavidin beads only / unstained bead autofluorescence for voltage, time gate and digital zero in AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750
* 1 x single-stain streptavidin-bead compensation control per reporter: AF350 single, GFP single, PE single, AF647 single, AF750 single

That is 1 + 5 = 6 bead tubes. Those six build the 5×5 spillover matrix on the same bead matrix we will sort on and define the unstained negative population. That is non-negotiable.

Where we differ is how many independent FMO gating controls are non-redundant for sorting on this specific panel.

For sorting we need spillover-aware positive/negative boundaries. That is normally FMO -X with the other four present. The question is whether the AF750-minus FMO adds information beyond the unstained bead baseline we already run.

In a streptavidin bead capture system AF750 is the far-red / dump channel. Its spillover into AF350, GFP, PE and AF647 is essentially negligible, and bead autofluorescence in the AF750 detector is very low. After compensation from the 5 single-stain beads, the residual signal in the AF750 detector from AF350+GFP+PE+AF647 is removed by the matrix we already built from the six compensation tubes.

In practice the AF750-minus tube, AF350+GFP+PE+AF647 with AF750 omitted, after proper compensation looks in the AF750 channel like the beads-only unstained control: the other four fluorochromes have been compensated out and the far-red bead background is the same as the unstained baseline we already acquired for voltage setting. The unstained beads-only control therefore already provides the all-minus reference and the AF750 background that the AF750-minus FMO would be meant to show.

The independent gating information is therefore for the channels where spillover from the other four fluorochromes actually moves the gate:
* FMO AF350- with GFP+PE+AF647+AF750
* FMO GFP- with AF350+PE+AF647+AF750
* FMO PE- with AF350+GFP+AF647+AF750
* FMO AF647- with AF350+GFP+PE+AF750

That is 4 non-redundant FMOs. Adding a fifth AF750-minus FMO duplicates the unstained/beads-only baseline we already have for autofluorescence, voltage and the all-minus reference.

So the essential, non-duplicative set for compensation plus spillover-defined sort gates on this bead panel is:
1 unstained/beads-only + 5 single-stain compensation beads + 4 independent FMOs = 10 tubes.

The 1+5+5 = 11 count is the textbook 2n+1 checklist and is what most core SOPs quote as best practice. As Colleague 10 notes, the formal 11 is 1+5+5 with the 10 practicable count being the same set with the all-minus condition collapsed into the unstained bead control. For a streptavidin bead sort with AF750 as a low-spillover dump channel, that collapse is real and the essential acquisition set is the 10 non-redundant controls.

For a streptavidin-bead capture sort the spillover matrix has to be built on the same bead matrix that is sorted on, and the gate has to be placed on spillover corrected data.

Compensation / instrument baseline minimum on beads
* 1 x streptavidin bead only / unstained bead autofluorescence baseline for voltage, threshold, time gate and digital zero in AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750
* 1 x single-stain streptavidin bead compensation control per detection channel that will be on the sorter

AF350-biotin on streptavidin beads
GFP-biotin on streptavidin beads
PE-biotin on streptavidin beads
AF647-biotin on streptavidin beads
AF750-biotin on streptavidin beads

= 1 + 5 = 6 bead tubes. Those six tubes are sufficient for a 5 × 5 spillover matrix for AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750 and to define an unstained bead negative population. That is the n+1 compensation minimum and the non-negotiable bead core.

That is not a sorting set. Compensation alone does not set a positive/negative sort boundary in the presence of spillover. For an unbiased sort gate the boundary in each detector must be defined with the other four fluorochromes present. That is the FMO control on the same bead matrix.

Sorting best practice on beads
* 1 unstained / beads-only
* 5 single-stain compensation beads as above
* 5 FMO bead tubes, one per channel, four fluorochromes present and the fifth omitted

FMO AF350- = GFP + PE + AF647 + AF750 on beads
FMO GFP-  = AF350 + PE + AF647 + AF750 on beads
FMO PE-   = AF350 + GFP + AF647 + AF750 on beads
FMO AF647- = AF350 + GFP + PE + AF750 on beads
FMO AF750- = AF350 + GFP + PE + AF647 on beads

1 + 5 + 5 = 11 tubes, the 2n+1 set for n = 5.

The six compensation/negative tubes are the absolute, non-negotiable minimum. The five FMOs are the standard essential addition for a sorting experiment because they allow spillover-aware gate placement in each of the five detectors. 

The 10-tube collapsed count 1 unstained + 5 singles + 4 independent FMOs is the same set with the AF750-minus FMO formally collapsed into the unstained bead baseline. The conventional core facility SOP and the 2n+1 teaching for a 5-colour sort quote the full 11 tube set, 6 of which are the strictly required compensation/bead baseline controls.

AF350-biotin, GFP-biotin, PE-biotin, AF647-biotin, AF750-biotin on beads

The AF750- FMO is AF350+GFP+PE+AF647 on streptavidin beads with AF750 omitted. The AF750 signal you see in that tube is therefore bead autofluorescence + background, i.e. the same baseline you already acquire with the unstained beads only control used for voltage setting and compensation.

Counting that as an independent acquisition double counts the all-minus reference. The unstained streptavidin bead control already provides the all-minus reference for every detector, and for AF750 it is functionally identical to the AF750-minus FMO in a bead capture assay. FMO AF350- with GFP+PE+AF647+AF750
FMO GFP- with AF350+PE+AF647+AF750
FMO PE- with AF350+GFP+AF647+AF750
FMO AF647- with AF350+GFP+PE+AF750

1 unstained/beads only + 5 single stain compensation beads + 4 independent FMOs = 10 essential, non-redundant acquisition tubes for compensation, autofluorescence baseline and spillover-aware sort gate placement on streptavidin beads.

The 1+5+5 = 11 count is the textbook checklist and is a useful best practice audit. In practice on this bead matrix the AF750-minus condition is covered by the beads-only control you already run, so the essential practical set is 10 tubes without losing compensation accuracy or FMO-defined gates.

1.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The question is about number of essential controls for a 5-channel Streptavidin-bead sort with AF350, GFP, PE, AF647, AF750.

Consensus stable across rounds:
* Compensation must be done on the same matrix that will be sorted, i.e. streptavidin beads.
* Minimal compensation-able set is n+1: 1 unstained/beads-only autofluorescence/baseline + 1 single-stain compensation control per fluorochrome.
* For 5 channels that is 1 + 5 = 6 bead tubes: unstained streptavidin beads + AF350 single, GFP single, PE single, AF647 single, AF750 single. These give autofluorescence baseline, voltage/threshold setting and a 5×5 spillover matrix. Singles are made by capturing biotinylated fluorochrome-conjugated reagents on streptavidin beads.

Disagreement persists about what “essential” means for a sorting experiment.

Strict compensation-minimum / 2n+1 camp, Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,16,17,18,3,4,6,7:
* Absolute non-negotiable minimum = 6 tubes.
* Best practice for sorting adds FMOs: 1 unstained +5 singles +5 FMOs = 11 = 2n+1.
* FMOs are standard essential for unbiased gate placement in presence of spillover. Colleagues 10,11,12,16,17,18 explicitly argue AF750-minus FMO is not equivalent to unstained because AF750-minus still contains AF350+GFP+PE+AF647 and shows spillover into AF750, whereas unstained shows zero signal. Unstained ≠ FMO.
* Formal essential sorting set is 11 tubes, 6 of which are strictly required compensation controls.

FMO-essential / collapsed-count camp, Colleagues 13,14,2,5,8,9:
* Argue FMOs are essential for sorting gate definition, not just best practice.
* Propose 1 unstained +5 singles +4 FMOs =10 controls.
* Rationale for collapse: the all-minus / FMO that lacks the last channel e.g. AF750-minus is essentially the unstained/beads-only baseline for this bead system. AF750 is far-red/dump/low spillover, its FMO does not add independent spillover information for gate setting, so AF750-minus is covered by unstained. Therefore non-redundant FMO set is AF350-, GFP-, PE-, AF647- only.
* Count: 1 +5 +4 =10, or 5 singles +5 FMOs =10 practicable controls with unstained counted as all-minus.

Intermediate statements:
* Colleagues 10,11,12,15,16,17,18 note formal count is 11, but 10 is often quoted when unstained is taken as the AF750-minus FMO.
* Colleague 11: 10-control count is same 1+5+5 set with all-minus FMO collapsed into unstained.
* Colleague 16: AF750-minus FMO still contains AF350/GFP/PE/AF647 signal and is therefore not equivalent to unstained beads-only; practical essential sorting set is 11.

Unresolved for me:
* Precise definition of “essential” in the question: strictly required to calculate compensation and run sorter =6, vs essential for reliable sort with properly placed gates = includes FMOs.
* Whether unstained control can be considered equivalent to the all-minus FMO and therefore counted only once. Majority of colleagues treat them as distinct; minority collapse for AF750.
* Additional best practice items like viability dye, isotype/biotin-blocked bead controls mentioned but not core to bead compensation debate.

Current understanding:
Minimal compensation-able set is unambiguously 6 bead tubes. The practical sort set most labs use is 11 tubes with FMOs. A middle position advocated by several colleagues is 10 essential controls when one FMO is merged with unstained, specifically AF750-minus. No corrections or factual errors spotted in channel list. Discussion has not shifted the fundamental n+1 consensus, only the FMO counting interpretation.

No new evidence contradicting earlier round. Belief remains that 6 is the strict minimum, 11 is the conventional teaching, 10 is the non-redundant practical claim for this panel because of AF750 dump channel.

12.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The question is about essential controls for a 5-channel streptavidin-bead sort with AF350, GFP, PE, AF647, AF750.

Consensus that persists:
* Bead-based compensation minimum is n+1 with n=5.
* 1 × unstained / streptavidin-bead only / beads-alone negative for autofluorescence, voltage/baseline and negative population.
* 1 × single-stain streptavidin-bead compensation control per fluorochrome: AF350 single, GFP single, PE single, AF647 single, AF750 single.
* That is 1 + 5 = 6 essential bead tubes for a 5×5 spillover matrix and for setting a negative gate. Described as non-negotiable minimum for compensation and instrument setup.

Disagreement / nuance about sorting gate controls remains stable.

Majority formal view in current round, Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,16,17,18,3,4,6,7:
* 6 tubes is absolute minimum, FMOs are best practice but additional.
* Formal best-practice total commonly quoted as 1 unstained +5 single-stain +5 FMO =11 tubes, 2n+1.
* FMO -AF750 is NOT redundant with unstained because FMO -AF750 still contains AF350+GFP+PE+AF647 and therefore shows spillover into the AF750 detector and spillover among the other four, whereas unstained shows zero fluorochrome.
* Keeping the all-minus condition distinct from channel-specific FMOs is the standard core-facility SOP.

Minority practical view, Colleagues 2,5,8,9,13,14:
* FMOs are essential for sorting gate placement and should be counted as essential.
* Propose 1 unstained +5 single-stain +4 FMOs =10 controls, with the AF750-minus FMO being effectively redundant with the unstained/beads-only baseline.
* Argument: AF750 is far-red/dump/low spillover; AF750-minus population after compensation is essentially bead autofluorescence, which is already provided by the unstained bead control. The unstained control already provides the all-minus reference for every detector.
* Independent FMO information is needed for AF350-, GFP-, PE-, AF647- where spillover moves the gate; AF750 gate is defined by unstained baseline.

Additional notes consistently raised:
* Additional controls often run but not part of core count: unstained cells, viability dye, isotype / biotin-blocked bead control for non-specific streptavidin binding.

Unresolved point remains definition of “essential”.
* If essential = strictly required to calculate compensation and define a negative reference → answer = 6.
* If essential = required to both compensate and set unbiased sort gates in presence of spillover → community splits between 10 with collapsed AF750-minus FMO and 11 with full n FMOs.
* Streptavidin bead matrix allows compensation set to be independent of cells, which drives discussion.

I am keeping both the 6-tube compensation minimum and the 10/11-tube sorting-best-practice sets as live options, noting the 4-FMO collapse argument for AF750 and the counter-argument that FMO -AF750 still contains four fluorochromes and is not identical to unstained.

* 1 x single-stain bead per reporter: AF350-biotin, GFP-biotin, PE-biotin, AF647-biotin, AF750-biotin
